Interpolation of q(x) estimates to a specific q(y) of interest

sbh_interpolation_complete.Rd

This function takes estimated q(x) values for a given region and uses linear interpolation through Coale-Demeny life tables to convert them all to a specific q(y) of interest (for their respective reference years). For example, if the q(x) estimates are obtained for a region and one is interested in reconstructing q(5) - U5MR over the reference years. The Coale-Demeny life tables can be found in the UN Guide to Estimation of Child Mortality, but are also embedded in the function for ease. For more information on the process and formulas, refer to the SBH_Demo vignette.

Usage

sbh_interpolation_complete(sbh_result_table, family, y)

Arguments

sbh_result_table

A dataframe with previously constructed q(x) estimates and their reference years for all age groups (i's) for one specific region. This can be obtained by using the sbh_brass_qx and sbh_brass_ti functions. Refer to the example below or the SBH_Demo vignette to view the process for obtaining such from SBH information. Columns should be named region, q_i, i, x, and ref_year exactly, with all except region being numeric. The dataframe should be 7 rows long.

family

A string field representing the family of Coale-Demeny life tables to be used (options: East, West, North, South - note this is case sensitive).

y

The under-y mortality rate of interest that all previous q(x)s will be interpolated to. This is NOT the same as i. For example, for U5MR (Under-5 Mortality) one should input y = 5 and not y = 4. Similarly, for under-10 mortality, you just input y = 10 and not y = 5. Recall previously in the q(x) functions however, you would input the i that corresponds to such mortality age.

Value

The sbh_result_table itself is returned with a new appended column representing the interpolated mortality rates for the y of interest.

Examples

# Example SBH data
sbh_example <- data.frame(
  region = rep("ExampleRegion", 7),
  i = 1:7,
  num_women = c(100, 110, 120, 130, 120, 100, 90),
  total_both = c(20, 80, 150, 220, 260, 240, 180),
  dead_both = c(2, 5, 9, 14, 18, 20, 17)
)

# Compute Brass q(x) estimates and reference years
region_name <- character(7)
ks <- numeric(7)
qs <- numeric(7)
yrs <- numeric(7)

for (i in 1:7) {
  result_brassq <- sbh_brass_qx(
    region_dataframe = sbh_example,
    i_brass = i,
    family = "West"
  )

  region_name[i] <- result_brassq$region
  ks[i] <- result_brassq$ki
  qs[i] <- result_brassq$qi

  yrs[i] <- sbh_brass_ti(
    region_dataframe = sbh_example,
    i_brass = i,
    family = "West",
    census_year = 2020
  )
}

# Create results table
sbh_results <- data.frame(
  region = region_name,
  q_i = qs,
  k_i = ks,
  i = 1:7,
  x = c(1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 15, 20),
  ref_year = yrs
)

# Interpolate all estimates to under-5 mortality
sbh_interpolation_complete(
  sbh_result_table = sbh_results,
  family = "West",
  y = 5
)
#> # A tibble: 7 × 7
#> # Rowwise: 
#>   region           q_i   k_i     i     x ref_year  q5_mr
#>   <chr>          <dbl> <dbl> <int> <dbl>    <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1 ExampleRegion 0.0843 0.843     1     1    2019. 0.119 
#> 2 ExampleRegion 0.0597 0.955     2     2    2017. 0.0684
#> 3 ExampleRegion 0.0576 0.959     3     3    2015. 0.0618
#> 4 ExampleRegion 0.0629 0.988     4     5    2013. 0.0629
#> 5 ExampleRegion 0.0701 1.01      5    10    2010. 0.0642
#> 6 ExampleRegion 0.0835 1.00      6    15    2008. 0.0719
#> 7 ExampleRegion 0.0938 0.994     7    20    2005. 0.0737
